this week's crawl had three threads worth pulling on if you build software for a living: infrastructure finally arriving in Africa, Kenya's digital policy machinery grinding through some genuinely messy rollouts, and a reminder that shipping an AI product means shipping an abuse problem too. plus Apple made a phone that folds, because of course it did.

## the data centers finally came home

Digital Realty just opened a 6.4 megawatt data center in Nairobi, and the financial press immediately started asking whether it's a smart bet ([simplywall.st](https://news.google.?oc=5), which followed up days later with a piece on whether the opening should move investor sentiment at all ([simplywall.st](https://news.google.?oc=5)). that's a modest facility by global standards, but it matters because it's proof that hyperscale capacity is finally landing on the continent instead of routing everything through Europe or the Gulf.

zoom out and the pattern gets bigger: Egypt just signed a reported one billion dollar data center deal with what's described as the world's most valuable company, part of a broader push where the US is outpacing China in African AI infrastructure ([Business Insider Africa](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Gulf Capital is reportedly circling African AI data center opportunities too ([Africa News Agency](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikAFBVV95cUxOdHRBZmhlVHJUSDZHdmFrdlpRT196bWd6aDJia2JSY0VRUEJoZWFtWWpXcnlmRmo0QWNQMWk4NWNxUjNDQUdPamd2X1NJRU9FWlJEVUs3UEl2elg0ZE9KRGVIV01FcTk3b0ZLbmdjTzI4MVZCSEltRmk5cndIQzZJZE9KcnRjZHE2bXN5dDVneXQ?oc=5)), while South Africa is reportedly feeling competitive pressure as the regional data center race heats up ([Yahoo](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxQVWdodVBWNno0RGd3MG5vRkkyTXowN1BZc1JpQlpXWi1ySU9sXzRaS1d1aWdlYXFmV2xMRXM0cGg3azhjOGRRNm5abE1sTFpGLXhwUC13SlgtN05WZDFVcGloV3JrQVlFODJUb1Z4azZvRFlscHRBQXlVN24zTDBvRGIydFcxNEprTVNxWEJGU3hFUQ?oc=5)). for context on how far behind the continent is starting, Finland alone has attracted over $30.2 billion in data center commitments from Google, Microsoft, and TikTok ([Yahoo Finance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxPb0JXY0k0RlZsRlRzcmtEOUdjbV8xeGZtMFZFVWNVVnhSdkFNOUh4VVR4OUp3M2FjZDVXanA2NHBhVS1uQ3hJMFdDNHlSWERBUkgtcHlPQzNhSmZ5TUpwNmJTcm12YVl6Nk8wMlJBRWFCeUc3ZWxBdGlhWjJSMXFLNnhPVi1sYzA1YTRnZFJWb0FZTWpNaWcyaS0wcw?oc=5). so a 6.4 MW site in Nairobi is a start, not a milestone, but it's the kind of start that lowers latency for anyone building for East African users and gives local companies a reason to stop shipping everything to Frankfurt. not every community welcomes this capacity expansion, though: petitioners in Wilmington are actively trying to block a proposed Amazon data center in their area, a reminder that power and water demands from these facilities are a local political fight everywhere, not just here ([WLWT](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxOOHFLN2tFVEd0TkVMX2w4VnB6Z3RjWGh3bWRDV1ZXZlBReUpicy1jWktReG5CcTRuWEpNVWFsMU1zUjY5d3MtQ2N2eXc5djRsMjFaMHRSSnZlTURETUpMU3pPMG0weFN0MkRJWW56dWpqVG5IZUNZUVBtOUN0ZGpKNzRDMTlabzF2Mzl0ajJMWC1uenBMbnNFRjdIMmx0bzR0c3pXb0ZmWUY?oc=5).

## kenya's digital plumbing is getting a messy upgrade

back home, the Communications Authority (CA) opened a public consultation on new network equipment rules that touch security, IPv6, artificial intelligence (AI), e-waste, accessibility, and performance standards ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/09/kenya-network-equipment-rules-consultation/)). if you build anything that talks to telecom infrastructure or imports networking gear, this is worth actually reading, not skimming.

meanwhile, KEMIS, the system replacing NEMIS as Kenya's learner records platform, is hitting technical problems that are colliding with Grade 10 school selection and raising real concerns about education funding accuracy ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/09/the-nemis-to-kemis-dilemma/)). this is a familiar story if you've ever migrated a production database with live users on it: the old system worked well enough that nobody budgeted for how hard the cutover would be.

on the threat landscape, Kenya's cyber attacks are reportedly up 6 percent even as ransomware incidents have nearly doubled globally ([Africa Business Communities](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxPallFSHBDdXR3Q3dXN0lrQjdvM1I1a1NjRWJFUHVQdm00NFR1Tl84N3NTaTI2dGFFMU9sREx2YkNnX1dmNHVzQkx3aW9QekpEQ2VlYy1WMG5WWllyYkZYNkFDUExtY1BmQ3d0NUJyd3VTZWZVSkM2dG80SFlXZjlnd3JVb1YyZXdnTzBEWU94Zm1SMlBDdElYNW83S2ZtZWJJRkpyVlUwU0k3V2xzRnU3OA?oc=5). that context makes NVIDIA and CrowdStrike's announcement of SafeMind, an agentic cybersecurity system unveiled at Fal.Con 2026, feel less like marketing and more like an admission: attacks are automated now, so defense has to be too ([NVIDIA](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-crowdstrike-fal-con-2026/)).

## when your chatbot gets recruited

Anthropic's latest threat report details how criminals, spies, propagandists, and even rival AI labs tried to weaponize Claude, its large language model ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/11/anthopic-claude-threat-report-ai-misuse/)). the Kenya-specific case in that report is worth sitting with: Anthropic says an operator used Claude to mass-produce political posts designed to look like organic grassroots opinion ahead of the 2027 elections ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/11/kenya-ai-claude-political-propaganda/)). if you're building anything with generative text output at scale, whether it's customer support replies or social content tools, assume someone will try to use it for astroturfing, and build your abuse detection before launch, not after a report calls you out by name.

## hardware roundup: a fold, a screen bill, and some quiet surveillance

Apple finally shipped its first foldable, the iPhone Duo, at $1,999 with a 7.6 inch display and a Split View multitasking mode ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/09/iphone-duo-foldable-phone/)), alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max with variable aperture cameras and a new A20 Pro chip ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/09/iphone-18-pro-and-max-launch/)), plus AirPods 5, Watch Series 12, and Watch Ultra 4 ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/09/apple-airpods-5-watch-series-12-health-features/)). Bloomberg had previewed the launch as a high stakes event before it happened ([Bloomberg](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixgFBVV95cUxOQUNobXZERmdnRHdVQ0xLdWRwYlNQMEJURmxDRUlqLVJWbWR0OEFxejlickp0VVhZUDZYSHY1cHNoRjd5NFpGMnBUUk1VTW1EU2xrSWpLcHBUdjNKWWJmQ0JDa1BGZHhtTVV2Y1Myb3pKRW5uYUlrSlhzYUtyZnVkVFhHLXJ0MzkwdnVXZXN1X1h5MkZRUzlkN01vaXEwOUZnbEd5SE5hZ0tIX2luMTZXdEltZUM5MFB6YnhMWmo3SEFibjN4Y1E?oc=5), TechRadar rounded up fifteen takeaways ([TechRadar](https://news.google.?oc=5), and Engadget did the full announcement breakdown ([Engadget](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilAFBVV95cUxNSVdmcG1mQU5wdkhpNW1VSXJCcHd5dHBETGxrUkZCQk4zVDFsc1FTUEl6NUNxNHVIQ0tUQXU2NlNqY1p1b3hJUjEtY1F1eW9Rb2s3czQtVzJUNTN0dHpfSVJxdkcyUFBkc25hNXpzMU9ib3BxVVEtT0ZEbEtMNGNWZXNyalFrYUhyamEzQ1BKazRsTTVq?oc=5). the interesting engineering detail is on the supply chain side: Apple is reportedly paying Samsung about $250 for every foldable screen, which goes a long way toward explaining that $1,999 price tag ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/11/iphone-duo-folding-screen-cost/)). a fold is still, apparently, an expensive hinge.

elsewhere in hardware you should actually worry about, an investigation reportedly found LG smart TVs scanning home networks and collecting device data even when the TV is supposedly off ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/09/lg-smart-tvs-network-scanning-privacy/)). if that's accurate, it is a strong argument for keeping smart TVs on an isolated VLAN or guest network at home, the same way you'd isolate any untrusted IoT device. on the more encouraging side, Google has made it easier for Android users to securely transfer passwords and passkeys between supported password managers, without exporting them as unencrypted plaintext files ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/10/android-password-manager-transfer/)). that's a small but genuinely useful piece of credential hygiene infrastructure most of us have been asking for.

last bit of local news: Absa Bank Kenya confirmed Yusuf Omari, a seventeen year veteran chief financial officer (CFO), as its new chief executive officer (CEO) after two months in an interim role ([Techweez](https://techweez.com/2026/09/10/absa-bank-kenya-ceo-yusuf-omari/)). worth watching if you work anywhere near Kenyan fintech or banking APIs, since new leadership often means new priorities for digital banking investment.
